problem: The answer labels ka = 6.28 as the optical region, but the chapter itself defines the optical region as ka ≫ 1 and the resonance/Mie region as ka around 1 to roughly 10. A sphere with ka = 6.28 (a = 0.1 m, λ = 0.1 m) sits at the upper end of the Mie/resonance region, not in the optical region. A student will memorise the wrong region boundary.
fix: Say: 'ka = 6.28, which puts the sphere at the upper end of the Mie/resonance region. Here σ is close to, but not exactly, the optical value; using σ ≈ πa² = 0.0314 m² (−15 dBsm) is a good approximation. The true optical region (σ = πa² exactly, no ripple) is reached only for ka ≫ 1.'

problem: 'The same aircraft nose may be in the Rayleigh region on a VHF radar' is inaccurate: an aircraft nose of about 1 m at VHF (λ of the order of 1–10 m) has ka near 1 to a few, which is the resonance region, not Rayleigh. Rayleigh needs the scatterer to be much smaller than a wavelength.
fix: Write: 'the same aircraft nose may be in the resonance region on a VHF radar and in the optical region on an X-band radar, with very different σ' (or, if Rayleigh is wanted, use a genuinely small feature such as a leading-edge strip or a small fastener).
